author: GamingBolt
description:
Tom Holland’s take on Peter Parker has just seen another memorable outing in Brand New Day, and a more personal examination of what it means to be the neighborhood-friendly Spider-Man in the vacuum of close friends that don't remember who the man under the mask truly is. 

But as good as that may be, we couldn’t help but look back to around three years ago, when we were busy helping Peter fight off the Venom symbiote after spending a good bit of time under its corrupting influence.

Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 continues to be the best take on the character as far as we’re concerned, and that’s not simply because of a great story involving all of his best supporting cast. We’ve got bigger reasons to like it, so join us on a look into why Insomniac continues to have the definitive version of the webslinging superhero there is.
title: Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 Is Still The Definitive Spider-Man Experience - Even After Brand New Day

author: GamingBolt
description:
“Crimson Desert has a new patch” would be the least shocking news of the week, especially since that's more or less been the case for almost five months straight. Think about all the monthly and then quarterly updates that No Man's Sky, The Division (1 and 2), Destiny 2, and so on received. That a single-player-only title – no co-op or online play whatsoever – has seen massive revamps almost weekly since its successful launch is practically unheard of, and it's garnered extensive appreciation.

However, this time it's different...or rather, it's a continuation of a more common trend. Last week saw a massive update that overhauled trading – 133 new trade posts, buffs to overall profit, trade routes on the map and mini-maps, dedicated tabs for viewing in-demand items from the map itself, new goods, the list goes on. But the most recent patch 1.17 includes bug fixes.
title: Crimson Desert Doesn't Need Another Massive Update, It Needs to Finish What It Started
